ALCALA Bik. 4A, Lot 16, H.V. Dela Costa Homes 11 Novaliches, Caloocan City Dear Mr. Alcala: S. This has reference to your letter dated 01 April 2018 requesting for the Department's opinion on the issue of whether or not the City of Caloocan is liable to pay for the electric consumption of streetlights in open spaces donated to it. Upon perusal of your letter and its attachments, the facts are as follows: The Freedom to Build Inc. (Developer), developer of H.V. Dela Costa Homes II Subdivision (Subdivision), donated the open areas of the Subdivision to the City of Caloocan by virtue of a Deed of Donation accepted through Sanggunian Resolution No. 1801 series of 2007. Despite such donation, the Homeowners Association of the Subdivision continues to pay for the electric consumption of the street lights installed in such open spaces. Consequently, upon request for Legal Opinion from the Office of the City Legal Officer of Caloocan City, it opined that: "While the City may have the responsibility to maintain donated roads and open spaces in a subdivision, this does not necessarily include the payment of electricity bills for street lights installed by the developer of a subdivision, especially if these street lights are for the exclusive use and benefit of the subdivision homeowners. Also upon request for a legal opinion from Housing and Land Use Regulatory Board, it opined that the City of Caloocan is responsible for the payment of the power consumption of street lights following the principle of accessories always follow the principal; the roads being the principal and the street lights being the accessories. Considering the above-stated facts, we find that the main issue is whether or not the City government of Caloocan is liable to pay for the street lights installed in the Subdivision open spaces donated to it. Our view is in the affirmative provided that the donation was executed and accepted in accordance with the law and its implementing rules and regulations. Presidential Decree No. 957 (PD 957), entitled as "Regulating the Sale of Subdivision Lots and Condominiums,

Providing Penalties for Violations Thereof", as amended by Presidential Decree No. 1216, is applicable. Section 31 thereof states: 'Sec. 31. Roads, Alleys, Sidewalks and Open spaces. The owner as developer of a subdivision shall provide adequate roads, alleys and sidewalks. For subdivision projects one (1) hectare or more, the owner or developer shall reserve thirty percent (30%) of the gross area for open space. such open space shall have the following standards allocated exclusively for parks, playgrounds and recreational use: (a) 99b of gross area for high density or social housing (66 to 100 family lot per gross hectare). (b) 7% of gross area for medium-density or economic housing (21 to 65 fåmily lot per gross hectare). (c) 3.5 07b of gross area low-density or open market housing (20 family lots and below per gross hectare). These areas reserved for parks, playgrounds and recreational use shall be non-alienablepublic lands, and non-buildable. The plans of the subdivision project shall include tree planting on such parts of the subdivision as may be designated by the Authority. Upon their completion as certified to ftv the Authority, Che roads. alleys. sidewalks and playgrounds shall be donated by the owner or developer to the cit or munici ali and it shall be mandato for the local overnmen ceuccepcprovided, however, that theparks and playgrounds may be donated to the Homeowners Association of the project with the consent of the city or municipality concerned. Noportion of the parks and playgrounds donated thereafter shall be converted to any other purpose or purposes. " (Emphasis supplied). Human Settlements Regulatory Commission Administrative Order No. 82-01, otherwise known as the "Rules and Regulations Implementing Sec. 31 of Presidential Decree No. 957 (IRR of PD 957), as amended by Presidential Decree No. 1216" also finds application. Section 8, 9, and IO thereof respectively state: "Section 8. Right of Grantee to Donate Road Lots and Open Space. Any person who is able to secure a Certificate of Completion from the Commission shall have the right to donate the road lots and open space to the City/Municipality concerned, provided that the parks, playgrounds and recreational use may be donated to the Homeowners Association of the subdivision with the consent of the City/MunicipaIity concerned.

Should the registered owner or developer merely secure a Certificate of Completion without making the corresponding deed of donation, he/she is still deemed responsible for the maintenance of the subdivision facilities in which case a reasonable amount of the performance bond shall be totally released by the Commission only upon showing by the registered owner or developer of proof of a deed of donation executed in favor of the City/Municipality concerned. "Section IO. Use of Donated Road Lots an Open Space. Road lots and open spaces donated by the owner or developer to the City/Municipality or to the Homeowners Association as the case may be shall not be converted to any purpose or purposes. In connection therewith, park, playgrounds and recreational uses and other similar facilities and amenities shall be non- alienable lands and no b ildin ors cture shall be built th reon o e than those which are. essential TQ the said open spaces as determined the "(Emphasis supplied). Republic Act No. 7160 (RA 7160), otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, particularly in Sections 458(5)(v) and 21, provide that the local government has the power to regulate the use of streets, avenues, alleys, sidewalks, bridges, parks and other public places and provide for their lighting, cleaning and sprinkling and that a local government unit may, pursuant to an ordinance, permanently or temporarily close or open any local road, alley, park or square falling within its jurisdiction. Thus, the local government is not precluded from regulating, opening or closing such spaces for the general welfåre of the public. Moreover, Section 17(2)(vii and viii) by way of paragraph Section 17(4) of RA 7160 mandates the City to exercise such other powers and discharge such other functions and responsibilities as are necessary, appropriate, or incidental to efficient and effective provision of the basic services and facilities which include public parks, playgrounds, sports facilities, infrastructure facilities intended primarily to service the needs of the residents including city roads, and other similar facilities. In light of the foregoing, our view is the fact that the Developer installed the subject street lights is moot and academic if the open spaces together with these street lights were validly donated to and accepted by the City government in accordance with the law and its implementing rules and regulation. If so, these open spaces and street lights have been

public properties for public use. As such, they are not meant for the exclusive use and benefit of the homeowners of the subdivision and are subject to regulation and maintenance by the local government. This view finds harmony with the principle of devolution of powers by which local governments are empowered to become effective partners in development. Section 2(a) of RA 7160 states: "(a) It is hereby declared the policy of the State that the territorial and political subdivisions of the State shall enjoy genuine and meaningfül local autonomy to enable them to attain their fullest development as self-reliant communities and make them more effective partners in the attainment of national goals. Toward this end, the State shallprovide for a more responsive and accountable local government structure instituted through a system of decentralization whereby local government units shall be given more povvers, authority, responsibilities, and resources. The process of decentralization shall proceed from the national government to the local government units. ' We hope that we have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, By the authority of the Secretary AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary MARIA LOURDES L AGUSTIN, CESOIII Regional Director DILG-NCR
